EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint, with US President Trump announcing mine clearance operations and a "zero tolerance" policy, while Iran and Oman negotiate a temporary maritime corridor, though Iran insists on stringent conditions for full reopening. Simultaneously, the US has signaled a shift away from new offensive strikes against Iran for now, focusing instead on economic pressure, amidst escalating internal economic hardship in Iran and a newly reported Iranian threat against Barron Trump.

IRAN
The status of the Strait of Hormuz (SoH) remains contentious. US President Trump announced that the US Navy has cleared all mines from the international waters of the SoH and warned Iran that any vessel laying new mines will be "immediately and systematically destroyed." He also stated that Space Force is monitoring the Strait, along with "Peacock Mountain" and three other "destroyed" nuclear sites. Conversely, Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi rejected the US minesweeping claim as "propaganda" and stated that the SoH will remain closed until Washington fulfills its commitments under the "Islamabad memorandum," which he claims the US violated by creating an "illegal southern route." Gharibabadi asserted that reopening the SoH is contingent on ending the war on all fronts, lifting the blockade, and resolving the situation in Yemen. Iran and Oman have discussed a "phased framework" for restoring safe navigation, including a temporary joint maritime corridor and joint mine-clearing, with technical talks for a permanent solution expected to last 30 to 60 days. Iran maintains full control over the entry route and part of the exit route. Reuters reported that only 5 ships transited the SoH on Tuesday, down from a daily average of 15, contributing to a 2% drop in Brent crude prices.

Internally, Iran faces severe economic distress. Multiple reports detail widespread fuel shortages across Tehran, Karaj, Tabriz, and Ardabil, with long queues at gas stations and some closures. The quality of fuel is also reported as poor. Soaring inflation has led to massive price increases for essential goods (e.g., potatoes, onions, cooking oil up 70 times since 2019), mobile phones, car repairs (e.g., 110 million Toman for a Peugeot 207 gearbox), and medical supplies (e.g., insulin up from 200,000 Toman to 8 million Toman for 25 units). The government is considering raising fuel prices, with Deputy Foreign Minister Ali Nikzad stating that while 60 liters at 1500 Toman will remain, other subsidized fuel allocations will be reduced. President Masoud Pezeshkian acknowledged economic shortcomings, stating the "war must end," while Parliament Speaker Mohammad-Baqer Qalibaf warned that the country would not endure if people are hungry. The US Secret Service is investigating an Iranian state TV video discussing a plot to assassinate Barron Trump, President Trump's son, including details of his movements and a purported $10 million bounty. NBC News reported "unprecedented damage" to US intelligence sites in West Asia from Iranian drones and missiles, with repair costs estimated in the billions. Ali Pishevarzadeh, a detainee from the January 2026 protests in Rasht, has been sentenced to death.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations continue in Gaza and against Lebanese targets. IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir visited Gaza, reaffirming the military's commitment to hunting down all terrorists involved in the October 7, 2023, attack, stating they "will live under pursuit until they are eliminated." Zamir emphasized that the IDF is prepared on all fronts and will not allow enemies in Gaza and Lebanon to rebuild their strength. In Gaza yesterday, the IDF and Shin Bet conducted strikes on five Hamas weapons depots located within mosques and near humanitarian infrastructure, along with a rocket launch site. Israeli Air Force strikes were reported in several locations in southern Lebanon, including Kfarmatta, Nabatieh, Ali Taher, al-Mansouri, Zarbin, al-Qantara, and Kfar Roman. An IDF force of over 10 vehicles was reported operating near the village of Jameleh in southwestern Syria. Israeli Defense Minister Yisrael Katz made an unannounced visit to Syria, stating that Israel would not withdraw from the Golan Heights and the security zone as long as "jihadi threats" persist, and affirmed actions against Turkish attempts to establish a presence in Syria.

A significant internal controversy erupted when far-right MK Zvi Sukkot smashed a "Martyrs' Monument" in the West Bank village of Madama during an IDF-approved tour. The IDF condemned Sukkot's actions as "deceptive and manipulative" and an "exploitation of security," emphasizing that it had already planned to demolish the monument. Prime Minister Netanyahu, Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar, and other prominent politicians, including Gadi Eisenkot and Naftali Bennett, strongly criticized Sukkot, with Netanyahu stating that public figures taking the law into their own hands is "wrong and interferes with the IDF." In domestic political news, the Likud party ordered a recount of ballots in Be'er Ya'akov due to suspected fraud. Yair Netanyahu, the Prime Minister's son, was reportedly secretly evacuated from Miami months ago and returned to Israel after an Iranian cell was detected tracking him. Ofer Winter launched a new right-wing political party, "Amcha Yisrael," intending to support a right-wing government, though Prime Minister Netanyahu urged him and others to unite with existing parties to avoid splitting votes.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In the Gaza Strip, the humanitarian situation is dire, with reports of a "horrific" hunger crisis due to the Israeli siege and "massive destruction" from the war. The IDF and Shin Bet carried out strikes yesterday, targeting five Hamas weapons depots (located inside mosques and near aid sites) and a rocket launch site, stating these facilities were used for terror activities. Dozens of "Israel-backed militia members" reportedly surrendered in Gaza. Israeli forces also reportedly raided and seized a UNRWA training center in Eastern al-Quds.

In the West Bank, the controversial smashing of a "Martyrs' Monument" by Israeli MK Zvi Sukkot in Madama village caused significant friction. The IDF condemned his actions, while Prime Minister Netanyahu and other officials criticized the unauthorized act. A cabinet meeting with PM Netanyahu convened to discuss concerns over potential escalation due to violence by "Jewish extremists" in the West Bank.

LEBANON
Israeli Air Force strikes were reported in several locations across southern Lebanon, including Kfarmatta, Nabatieh, Ali Taher, al-Mansouri, Zarbin, al-Qantara, and Kfar Roman. IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir stated that the IDF is vigilant on the Lebanese front and "will not allow our enemies...to rebuild their strength." No direct reports of Hezbollah operations were specified in the intelligence feed.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In a significant development for Syria, Mazloum Abdi, the Commander-in-Chief of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), announced the official dissolution of the organization and its autonomous Kurdish administration. Abdi stated that the SDF forces are now fully integrated into Syrian state institutions and the Syrian army, with reports indicating he has been appointed as a special advisor to Abu Mohammad al-Jolani, the head of the Syrian government, for Kurdish affairs. This follows meetings between Syrian President al-Shara and the SDF commander in Damascus. In southern Syria, an Israeli IDF force, consisting of over 10 vehicles, was reported operating in the area of Jameleh village. Israeli Defense Minister Yisrael Katz made an unannounced visit to Syria, reiterating that Israel would not withdraw from the Golan Heights and a security zone as long as "jihadi threats" persist, and confirming actions against Turkish attempts to establish a presence in Syria. Turkish President Erdogan affirmed Turkey's commitment to supporting its neighbors and pursuing peace and stability in the region, rejecting external dictates on its foreign policy.

In Iraq, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad-Baqer Qalibaf met with Faiq Zidan, the head of Iraq's Supreme Judicial Council, emphasizing the decisive role Iran and Iraq can play in shaping a new regional order. The Iraqi Interior Ministry successfully seized 36 kilograms of Captagon pills and arrested traffickers. The Iraqi National Security Service arrested an individual who had impersonated officials, including the Prime Minister, to gain personal benefits. Barzani militias were reported storming homes of the Harkiya people in Erbil province without legal warrants. The Japanese JGC company is expected to resume work on the FCC project in Basra by early September.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia's cabinet, led by King Salman, underscored the critical importance of keeping the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab open and secure, advocating for stable diplomatic solutions and freedom of navigation. The US Trump administration has submitted a civilian nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress, though President Trump insists that the agreement's progress is contingent on Saudi Arabia joining the Abraham Accords and recognizing Israel.

Oman is playing a key diplomatic role in the Strait of Hormuz situation. Its Foreign Minister, Badr al-Busaidi, visited Tehran and engaged in discussions with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, leading to the announcement of a "phased framework" for restoring safe navigation, which includes establishing a temporary joint maritime corridor and implementing a joint mine-clearing project. Al-Busaidi expressed optimism for an imminent announcement on practical arrangements for safe navigation.

Qatar's Foreign Minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, held a telephone conversation with Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi, with both sides emphasizing the importance of diplomatic channels to prevent regional escalation. Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesperson reiterated that US sanctions against Iran are unilateral and that Qatar supports ongoing mediation efforts.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Strait of Hormuz Controversy:** US President Trump announced the US Navy cleared all mines from the international waters of the Strait of Hormuz, threatening immediate destruction for any new mining. Iran's Deputy FM Kazem Gharibabadi rejected this as "propaganda," stating the Strait remains closed until US fulfills commitments.
2.  **Iran-Oman Temporary Corridor Deal:** Iran and Oman announced discussions for a temporary joint maritime corridor and mine-clearing in the Strait of Hormuz, with technical talks for a permanent system expected in 30-60 days.
3.  **US Shift on Iran Strikes:** US Secretary of State Marco Rubio indicated the US is unlikely to initiate new offensive strikes against Iran "for now," prioritizing economic pressure and maritime security until at least the November midterm elections.
4.  **Iranian Economic Crisis:** Widespread fuel shortages, long queues at gas stations, skyrocketing prices for basic goods, and business closures are reported across Iran, exacerbating internal economic hardship.
5.  **SDF Dissolution in Syria:** Mazloum Abdi, Commander-in-Chief of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), announced the official dissolution of the SDF and its autonomous administration, with forces integrating into the Syrian state and army. Abdi is reportedly appointed as an advisor to Syrian government head Abu Mohammad al-Jolani.
6.  **Israeli MK's Controversial Act:** Israeli MK Zvi Sukkot smashed a "Martyrs' Monument" in the West Bank village of Madama during an IDF-approved tour, drawing strong condemnation from PM Netanyahu, other officials, and the IDF for deceptive conduct.
7.  **Iranian Threat Against Barron Trump:** The US Secret Service confirmed awareness of an Iranian state TV video discussing a plot to assassinate Barron Trump, President Trump's son, detailing movements and a purported $10 million bounty.
8.  **CIA Director's Moscow Visit:** CIA Director John Ratcliffe made an unannounced, four-hour visit to Moscow, reportedly to deliver an "ultimatum" to Russia regarding drone incursions into NATO territory.
9.  **Canadian Retaliatory Tariffs:** Canada announced tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on approximately $20 billion worth of US goods, including doubling tariffs on steel, in response to new US tariffs.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The primary flashpoint remains the Strait of Hormuz, with conflicting narratives from the US and Iran and Trump's "zero tolerance" policy creating a high risk of kinetic engagement if new mines are detected or perceived. Iran's severe internal economic crisis poses a significant risk of increased public unrest and potential government instability, while its acting Defense Minister views economic pressure as an act of war, hinting at potential retaliation. The IDF's continued hunt for October 7 terrorists in Gaza and Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon suggest ongoing operational activity and a high potential for renewed escalation on both fronts. The unannounced CIA visit to Moscow to deliver an "ultimatum" to Russia regarding drone incursions into NATO territory highlights the potential for the Ukraine conflict to lead to direct US-Russia confrontation, with Canada's retaliatory tariffs also indicating rising international trade tensions.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **United States** has indicated a strategic shift towards Iran, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio stating new offensive strikes are unlikely "for now," focusing instead on economic pressure and ensuring navigation in the Strait of Hormuz until at least the November midterm elections. President Trump confirmed the US Navy's mine clearance in the Strait and issued a "zero tolerance" warning. The Trump administration also submitted a civilian nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress, contingent on KSA recognizing Israel. CIA Director John Ratcliffe conducted an unannounced visit to Moscow to deliver an ultimatum to Russia regarding drone incursions.

**Gulf States** responses vary: **Saudi Arabia** emphasized the importance of maintaining open and secure waterways in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, supporting diplomatic solutions. **Oman** is actively mediating, engaging Iran in discussions for a temporary joint maritime corridor and mine-clearing in the Strait. **Qatar** expressed support for mediation efforts and viewed US sanctions on Iran as unilateral, emphasizing diplomatic channels to prevent escalation.

**China** "firmly opposes" US unilateral sanctions against Iran, asserting that its cooperation with Tehran is within international law and should not be disrupted. China also warned it would retaliate against any major expansion of US secondary sanctions targeting Chinese companies.

**Russia** reported shooting down 426 Ukrainian drones and confirmed the CIA Director's visit for intelligence agency coordination. Russia also launched attacks on cargo ships and an oil tanker in Black Sea ports.

**Turkey's** President Erdogan emphasized national interests and continued support for neighbors, asserting Turkey's independent foreign policy in the region and implying rejection of external pressure.

The **United Kingdom's** Treasury Secretary stated continued economic pressure on Iran alongside the US and partners, having imposed over 240 sanctions, and welcomed increased pressure to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

**Pakistan's** Army Chief Asim Munir engaged in high-level diplomacy in Tehran, reportedly proposing the US lift its naval blockade and sanctions in exchange for Iran ceasing proxy attacks. Pakistan has also requested a $10 billion loan from the US Treasury.

**Canada** announced retaliatory tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on approximately $20 billion worth of US goods, escalating a trade dispute.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Contradictions persist regarding the Strait of Hormuz: US President Trump declared the Strait cleared of mines, yet Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi dismissed this as "propaganda" and reiterated its closure until US conditions are met, suggesting ongoing significant disagreement. Oman's Foreign Minister's statements about a "temporary corridor" and "practical arrangements" indicate ongoing negotiations rather than a resolved situation.

The US diplomatic posture is mixed; while Secretary of State Rubio suggested a shift away from new offensive strikes, and there are reports of diplomats returning to Middle Eastern embassies, these moves contrast with aggressive rhetoric from President Trump and the reported threat against his son by Iranian state TV.

Unverified claims include Omid Dana's report of "tank movements towards IRGC headquarters in Iranshahr/Chabahar." The "Al-Hadath Saudi Channel" claim that Pakistan's Army Chief Munir delivered a "surrender" message from Trump and that Iran vowed to continue fighting if escalation occurs is significant but should be assessed with caution given the source's potential agenda.

Propaganda is evident in both Iranian and US statements. Iranian officials frame economic hardship as a "humanitarian crisis" caused by US sanctions, while Trump's rhetoric about Iran's "collapsing" economy and "killing protesters" serves to justify US pressure. The Iranian state TV threat against Barron Trump could be a form of psychological warfare.

Reporting gaps exist concerning the specifics of "jihadi threats" in Syria cited by Israeli Defense Minister Katz and details of the alleged Iranian assassination attempt on Yair Netanyahu. The full implications of the SDF's rapid dissolution and integration into the Syrian government on regional stability and Kurdish autonomy also remain to be seen.
